The edition's own statement of rights (from eBible.org's page for this translation, https://ebible.org/awk/copyright.htm):
> The Gospel According to Luke in the Awabakal language of Australia
> Public Domain
> Language: Awabakalkoba (Awabakal)
> 2020-03-03

Why this is public domain:
Translator: Lancelot Edward Threlkeld, 1788-1859; editor: John Fraser, 1834-1904. Text: part 2 of "An Australian Language as Spoken by the Awabakal", Sydney, Government Printer Charles Potter, 1892. US: published before 1931. Australia: life plus 70 years; Fraser died in 1904, so the term ended in 1974.

The verse-per-line archive holds the Bible text in one file, one verse per line, each line starting with its reference (book, chapter:verse); its SQL and XML copies of the same text, eBible.org's description page, style sheet and signature are left out of the source.

Sources of these facts: eBible.org's details page (https://ebible.org/details.php?id=awk), the edition's copyright page (https://ebible.org/awk/copyright.htm), https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lancelot_Threlkeld; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Fraser_(ethnologist); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_countries%27_copyright_lengths; https://copyright.cornell.edu/publicdomain.
